txt: Patrol Officer Minot picks it up and gives it back to you -- slippery and cold.
She listens to you sadly. The wind blows.
She nods, then looks down at her hands. No frostbite, sure, but a web of thin red cracks around the wrists. She is visibly embarrassed by the delicacy of her skin.
Suddenly, she smiles at some thought that had just come to her, nods to the surgeon again, and sprints down the stairs, gloveless, into the falling snow.
"... get back to it. We left Torson and McLaine to run the C-Wing. It's not good."
"A detective *and* a civilian. Jean -- *and* the gun. He has it..."
"And we also have a huge case load, lieutenant," she says with a smile. "Piles that we need to get back to. Mountains, even."
"Anything that ends the *trial* is okay with me." A quick nod.
"Before you were a cop, you were a gym teacher in Couron." She looks around. "It's getting really cold outside. Should we maybe..."
"But, Detective Vicquemare," she interjects. "He *has* blanked out before."
"Cuno -- please. If it's on the island, then it will be seen again. Calm down..."
"Detective -- please. Don't start talking about your *pheromones* again. This is serious. If you don't..." She doesn't finish the sentence.
"Detective Vicquemare... I'm not saying he's the Son of Lung. But lying? I mean -- he *has* blacked out before..."
"Detective Vicquemare... he *has* blacked out before. We should take this seriously."
"Detective." She looks at Vicquemare. "I just don't want this *trial* to go on any longer. It's cold outside, and... let's just go."
"Detective." She looks at Vicquemare. "I just don't want this *trial* to go on any longer. It's cold outside, and..."
"For god's sake..." She sighs. "Yes, we'll do it."
"Fuck it -- I believe him." She looks at Vicquemare and shrugs.
"God... Calm down, Jean."
"Good." She looks at you, then Vicquemare...
"Harry, we want to help you. Trant, I believe this is where you come in?"
"Harry, we're here because we're worried."
"He found it!" The patrol officer picks it up and gives it back to you -- slippery and cold. "He found it, Jean. It's his badge!"
"He found it. It's his badge. I can confirm."
"He has... That's true."
"He's telling the truth. You were a gym teacher in Couron." She looks around. "It's getting really cold outside. Should we maybe..."
"Hi."
"Honestly -- anything that ends this *trial* is okay with me." A quick nod.
"I just know we can't give up on him when he's at his weakest. He wouldn't..." The crowd in the room has started fidgeting uncomfortably. Someone's trying to slip out unnoticed.
"It *is* what a soldier of the ICM would be called."
"It is... it *is* getting cold out..." She looks around -- at the dilapidated fishing village.
"It wasn't like that..."
"It's a clean win."
"It's good to meet you, Lieutenant Kitsuragi," she says warmly, flashing the lieutenant the tiniest of smiles.
"It's okay," she sighs. "I didn't come here to gloat, or to fool you. Neither did he, actually." She gestures toward Vicquemare. "We're just worried."
"Jamrock is the largest ghetto in Revachol. Faubourg, technically... but it's divided into *eleven* districts. Jamrock only has us."
"Jean -- I think he hasn't. I can see it on his face..."
"Jean -- it *is* his style."
"Jean -- it's his style. He does side cases. I'm sure it was important enough. Call it community outreach."
"Jean, maybe..." She stops and sighs.
"Jean, stop brutalizing him... He's trying."
"Jean. He has it. No more cooperation needed. He had a civilian there for the confession -- this is doable."
"Jean..." She stops.
"Lieutenant, please -- you have to have more than just some *mantis*. The straggler -- stick to that. You said you solved the murder."
"Lieutenant, please. The straggler -- just... stick to that. You said you *solved* the case?"
"Lieutenant," she says with a heavy sigh. "My name is not 'Horse-Faced Woman'. It's Judit Minot. I was assigned to your unit two months ago. I thought we were friends..."
"Lieutenant. Really... I..."
"Look..." She turns to face the sea. "It's about to rain soon. It's time to go home."
"Look..." She turns to face the sea. "It's raining. It's time to go home."
"Look..." She turns to face the sea. "The sun is about to go down. It's time to go home."
"Look..." She turns to face the sea. "The sun is going down. It's time to go home."
"Mack 'The Torso' Torson and Chester McLaine --" She arches an eyebrow. "They're not fit to run a wing. Believe me. Things are shaky as it is."
"No. Thank you. I got it." She gets the umbrella to open, and, with a quick smile and nod to the surgeon, sprints down the steps. The rain falls all around her...
"No." She shakes her head. "Without *any* benefits."
"Of course." She turns to Vicquemare. "Call it community outreach, right?"
"Okay." Another sigh. "Because you're my commanding officer. I... I really want to respect you. I want us to have a normal relationship."
"Okay." Another sigh. "You're my commanding officer. I... I really want to respect you. I want us to have a normal relationship."
"Ptolemy Pryce? He's the son of the old Pryce -- one of the founders of the RCM."
"Right, sir." Her tone is suddenly very cold.
"See? He really *doesn't* remember. It wasn't a 'sick joke' -- at least that's good."
"See?"
"So it *is* connected...?"
"So... it *is* what a soldier of the ICM would be called."
"Speak up, lieutenant," she tries to reassure you. "It's okay. I believe there was a straggler."
"Still," she says quietly. "Good work with the missing person, detective."
"Tabernacle? It's on the way over. Near where you live, on Perdition..." She looks at Vicquemare.
"Talks concluded?" She hugs herself for warmth.
"That's not true..."
"The body was transported to Precinct 41. Our morgue. I had Tillbrook and Mollins take care of funeral arrangements and family-stuff."
"They're not going to go for this speculation in the Constabulatory."
"This isn't cause for celebration. It's... bad."
"This would really help with some of the... *problems* we've been having."
"Uhm, and..." She looks around. "People on this street helped us too. With your whereabouts."
"Uhm, and..." she interjects, trying to defuse the situation. "People on this street helped us too."
"Vic, calm down..."
"We must help him." Minot looks down at her neatly polished black shoes. There is a quiet firmness to her voice when she speaks.
"We've read the reports, Harry. Lieutenant Kitsuragi's. We know."
"We've read the reports. Lieutenant Kitsuragi's. We know."
"What is going on here? Did something happen?" she asks, startled. Jean Vicquemare turns to her and says...
"Where are hell are they..." she mutters under her breath.
"Wonderful," the woman looks north. "Then can we please just go back to Jamrock now?"
"Yes, a couple of times. After some of the more... serious benders." She pauses, remembering. "One was after the Two Drunks case, the other when we looked into that mural."
"You haven't told us about that -- you've just told us about being a gym teacher."
